title: How Long Do Dental Crowns Last: Realistic Lifespans & Care
seoTitle: How Long Do Dental Crowns Last? Lifespan by Material
seoDescription: Crowns typically last 5 to 15 years, longer with the right material and care. See lifespans by type and tips to extend them. Ask our Valencia team.
excerpt: Typical crown lifespans by material, the reasons crowns fail early, and a practical checklist to help yours last longer.
keyTakeaways: Crowns typically last 5 to 15 years; many function well for 10 to 20 years with good hygiene, a stable bite and regular care.
By material: porcelain-fused-to-metal 5–15 years, all-ceramic 8–15, monolithic zirconia 10–20+, gold alloy 15–30+.
Lifespan depends on remaining tooth structure, material, oral habits and hygiene, and the quality of fit and cementation.
A crown that keeps coming off usually signals too little tooth structure or a poor fit; a new crown alone rarely fixes it.
Ask for an itemized estimate and insurer pre-authorization before treatment; forum reports of surprise balances are common.
